sources_considered.why: Report on day 1 of the Kaggle/DeepMind LLM chess tournament (Aug 5, 2025). Documents illegal-move forfeits and board-tracking weaknesses.
June 2025 report on ChatGPT losing track of a chess board against Atari Video Chess.
ICML 2025 paper on whether foundation models learn world models. Used as context because it studies purpose-trained models, not chat LLMs.
Final results only. Nothing further on illegal moves.

receipt.public_excerpt: The Gemini 2.5 Pro vs. Claude 4 Opus match was the only one to have more games finishing by checkmate than by illegal move forfeits.

evidence_items.explanation: In a tournament of eight leading LLMs, most first-round matches had more games lost to illegal moves than to checkmate. This matches Marcus's own example of failing to stick to legal moves.

receipt.public_excerpt: So far, LLMs have displayed three key weaknesses when it comes to playing chess: visualizing the entire board, understanding how pieces interact with each other, and making legal moves

evidence_items.explanation: The tournament report names board-state tracking and legal moves as general LLM weaknesses in August 2025.

receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT confused rooks for bishops, missed pawn forks, and repeatedly lost track of where pieces were—first blaming the Atari icons as too abstract to recognize, then faring no better even after switching to standard chess notation.

evidence_items.explanation: This is an informal but documented June 2025 test. In it, ChatGPT 4o repeatedly lost track of the board state.

receipt.public_excerpt: For now, Grok 4 has shown that it doesn't share the same limitations.

evidence_items.explanation: At least one model avoided these failures on day 1. This shows the weakness was not universal across all leading models.

receipt.public_excerpt: So far, foundation models are not capable of making the transition humans are capable of making: from good predictions to accurate world models.

evidence_items.explanation: This peer-reviewed finding says foundation models tend to learn task heuristics rather than world models. It is context only, because it studies models trained on specific domains, not chat LLMs.

unresolved_gaps: No systematic summer 2025 benchmark of world-state tracking across all frontier LLMs was found. The chess evidence comes from one tournament and one informal test.
Earlier research (e.g., on Othello and chess-trained transformers) suggests some internal world representations exist. That does not settle whether they are 'stable'.
The 'number of limbs' example was not independently checked.
